gateway_client.code_ref: engine route: waav-infer/crates/waav-infer-server/src/lib.rs:1598-1765 (POST /v1/audio/transcriptions); gateway request code to extract: gateway/src/handlers/transcribe.rs:769-814 and :947-1027
gateway_client.notes: Request restrictions enforced by the engine, each answered with HTTP 400 (unsupported_param): a non-empty language or prompt (lib.rs:1564-1574, :1663-1676); any response_format other than json or text, so verbose_json fails (lib.rs:1704-1715); any temperature other than 0 (lib.rs:1576-1596). The model field must be empty or name the loaded family, otherwise model_not_found (lib.rs:1647-1662; engine.rs:2750-2764). Unknown fields such as stream are read and ignored. The response is {"text": ...} only: no timestamps, no confidence, no detected language. Send 16 kHz audio, because the engine otherwise resamples linearly. Limits are the engine defaults (lib.rs:144-166, :48): 100 MiB upload, 64 concurrent requests, a 2 second wait for admission and then HTTP 429 with code admission_rejected, a 30 second deadline per request. A 429 from the engine is load shedding and must not count as a failure for the circuit breaker (gateway/src/core/resilience/infer_reject.rs). Concurrent uploads are folded into one batched forward pass of up to 24 clips with no added delay (waav-infer-server/src/stt_coalescer.rs:26-33, :142-145). The engine binds loopback with no authentication by default and serves one speech-to-text model per process.

transport.disabled_reason: Not implemented. The gateway has no speech-to-text client for the OpenAI Realtime transcription session. Its only code for that socket is a pass-through relay for customers who speak the Realtime protocol themselves, which cannot feed the gateway's own speech-to-text, language-model and text-to-speech chain. Decisions section 12 places the commit transport for OpenAI only.

gateway_client.code_ref: relay only: gateway/src/handlers/openai_realtime/upstream.rs:113-191 (builds {base}/realtime?intent=transcription for openai and /openai/v1/realtime?intent=transcription with an api-key header for azure_openai); session and event types to reuse: gateway/src/core/realtime/openai/protocol.rs
gateway_client.notes: How the session must work: open the socket with intent=transcription; send session.update with session.type set to transcription, input format audio/pcm at 24 kHz (the gateway must resample from the caller's rate), the transcription model, and turn_detection null; append base64 audio continuously; when the gateway's own voice detector decides the utterance has ended, send input_audio_buffer.commit. Text arrives as conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta while the caller speaks and as ...completed after the commit. Completions for different turns may arrive out of order and must be matched by item_id. A commit on an empty buffer is an error. The live models reject the vendor's own voice detection, which is why the gateway owns endpointing here. The intent=transcription query is what the gateway relay, Pipecat and LiveKit dial and what Microsoft's sample uses; it is absent from OpenAI's own pages. The language and context fields are left out of this profile because they differ by model (languages and keywords on gpt-live-transcribe, language and no prompt on gpt-realtime-whisper) and a profile cannot see the model.

gateway_client.notes: Socket ws://host/v1/realtime, read from vLLM source at commit bc21cba. The server sends session.created with an id and no session object. The client must send session.update {model} before anything else; the documentation calls it optional but the code rejects a commit without it (model_not_validated), and a valid update is not acknowledged. Audio is input_audio_buffer.append with base64 PCM16 at 16 kHz mono and nothing else, so the gateway must resample. input_audio_buffer.commit has the opposite meaning to OpenAI's: it starts generation and is sent before the audio; commit with final true ends the audio. A second commit while generation runs is ignored. Text arrives as transcription.delta (append-only) and transcription.done; errors carry a string, not an object. There is no voice detection on the server, so the gateway decides where a turn ends. The route exists only when the loaded model supports the realtime task (Voxtral Realtime and the Qwen3-ASR realtime class); otherwise the upgrade fails with HTTP 403, which looks like a permission error. The Qwen3-ASR class emits text only once per 5 second block, so for conversation it is no better than the file path. vLLM does not reclaim idle streaming sessions, so every open call holds capacity.

gateway_client.notes: Socket ws://host:9000/v1/realtime?intent=transcription; a missing or wrong intent closes the socket with code 1008. The first server frame is conversation.created, not session.created. The client configures with transcription_session.update (input_audio_format pcm16, sample rate 16000 by default, model, BCP-47 language, prompt, endpointing_config, word_boosting), sends input_audio_buffer.append, and may send commit, clear and done. Text arrives as conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta and .completed, the latter with words_info, vad_states and is_last_result. Server defaults: sessions expire after 3600 seconds, close after 60 seconds without activity, at most 100 connections, messages up to 10 MB (the page also says 15 MB per append; plan for the smaller). An optional single-use token expires 60 seconds after it is issued. Streaming works only when the container was started with a streaming profile; Whisper, Canary and Parakeet TDT are offline only, Nemotron ASR Streaming and Parakeet CTC or RNNT have streaming profiles. Recorded as endpointing by either side with a silence signal because the session has an endpointing configuration and reports voice states; that reading is an inference and whether the server finalises a segment without a client commit was not confirmed. word_boosting may map to key terms; that mapping is not decided.

gateway_client.notes: A vendor-side segmenting facade: a socket that accepts live audio but runs a batch model once per utterance behind it. Socket /v1/realtime?model=...&intent=transcription&language=...&transcription_model=..., read from speaches source at commit 993994f. The route exists for every model. Incoming audio is treated as 24 kHz and resampled to 16 kHz by the server. The session uses the older OpenAI beta shape (input_audio_transcription.model, turn_detection.type server_vad), not the current session.type transcription shape. Server voice detection defaults: threshold 0.9, no prefix padding, 550 ms of silence. On speech stop or on a client commit the buffer is written to a WAV file and sent to the server's own file transcription; one conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed is published and no delta event. A committed buffer must hold at least 100 ms; a session lasts at most 30 minutes. Authentication is a Bearer header, an X-API-Key header or an api_key query parameter, and no OpenAI-Beta header. response.cancel and conversation.item.truncate are not supported. Whether turn detection can be switched off so that only the gateway commits was not confirmed.

The Deepgram streaming client can already dial another host, but a self-hosted deployment has no route to it: there is no factory arm for this vendor, no trusted channel that carries the deployment's base address to speech-to-text, and the client-settable address override is rejected for in-cluster hosts by the private-address filter.

gateway_client.code_ref: gateway/src/core/stt/deepgram.rs:465-480 (build_websocket_url appends /v1/listen to endpoint_override); override check at gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:366-381
gateway_client.notes: For a server that speaks Deepgram's live socket at {base}/v1/listen: a self-hosted Deepgram engine, or WhisperLiveKit, whose /v1/listen is documented as a compatibility subset (interim_results, is_final, speech_final, KeepAlive and CloseStream are supported; Finalize is not). The gateway's Deepgram client never sends Finalize; it closes the stream instead, which fits the subset. WhisperLiveKit fixes raw audio at 16 kHz, while the gateway forwards the caller's bytes unchanged at whatever rate the caller sent (gateway/src/core/voice_manager/manager.rs:634-639) and only declares that rate in the URL (deepgram.rs:498), so audio at any other rate must be resampled first or the transcript is garbage with no error. Behind this socket WhisperLiveKit re-decodes a growing window with Whisper, so latency and GPU cost differ from a natively streaming model. Using this route for streaming Whisper is an idea from the research, not a tested path; no quality signal or context field is assumed.
